newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Thursday, although some traders expected the market to continue to recover from Wednesday's lows.
"I think it is a bit oversold," said one dealer.

New York arabicas ended mixed on Wednesday, after an early speculative-led sell-off. September tumbled to a session low of 177.50 cents per lb, but closed at 183.10 cents, down 5.10 cents. December fell 3.00 cents, to 165.50 cents, while the back months closed down 0.65 to up 1.60 cents.
September/December narrowed to 17.60 cents compared with 19.70 cents at the close on Tuesday.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 185.00-186.00 cents, followed by Wednesday's high of 188.50 cents. On the downside, support was seen at 180.00 cents, then 177.50 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday that no damaging cold weather is expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt. Low temperatures will be in the 50s to low 60s F (low to middle teens C).
WSC also said showers have improved the outlook for the developing and maturing coffee crops in parts of Mexico, Central America and Colombia.

After Wednesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 606 60-kg bags as of August 12, to 92,959 bags. There were an additional 5,853 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

In other news, the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) said in a statement released late Wednesday that green coffee exports totaled 1.03 million 60-kg bags in July according to the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
This was down 12 percent from the 1.18 million bags shipped in the same month last year but Abecafe is still anticipating total shipments in 1997 to reach 16.5 million bags, up 27 percent from 1996.

London robusta futures were weaker in quiet trade early Thursday, but off lows. LIFFE September fell $12 at the midday break, to $1,498, after ranging from $1,510 to $1,485. November was down $16, to $1,510.
